correctness.rationale: Each crown vertex has degree n-1; the ordinary defensive inequality reduces to y-1_(i in Y)>=t=floor((n-1)/2) on selected a_i and analogously on b_i. For overlap r=0 both occupancies >=t; if r>0 both >=s=t+1. Removing one vertex proves locally minimal iff (r=0,x=y=t) or (r>=2,x=y=s); removing a suitable pair across the common indices proves globally minimal iff the latter overlap has r>=3. Exact labeled choices D=C(n,t)C(n-t,t), H(n,r)=C(n,s)C(s,r)C(n-s,s-r) yield the two polynomials, parity binomial-square simplifications, and Stirling tail proportions. Checked n=3,4 exceptions, disjoint/overlapping cases, and meaning of inclusion globally minimal vs dominating. Independent direct adjacency-mask enumeration checked all nonempty subsets, single-deletion and arbitrary-subset minimality for n=3..7 (not inferred solely from formula).
